verdict.tagline: Tactical gunplay battles crashes, connection drops, and erratic artificial intelligence.
for_you_if: you want slow-paced tactical breaching mechanics
you enjoy dark and raw law enforcement themes
you can coordinate with a dedicated multiplayer squad
not_for_you_if: you lack patience for technical crashes and bugs
you need reliable multiplayer connections without disconnects
you expect responsive artificial intelligence teammates and suspects

As much as the game may actually be alright, I feel I can't give a positive review for three reasons:

1) First and foremost, THE USE OF GENERATIVE AI
In some missions, some decoration elements are blatantly made with generative AI. This might not seem like a big deal since it's not something major, but VOID Interactive has more than enough money to hire ACTUAL artists. If they were just used as placeholders during development and then replaced with real art it would've been understandable, but either they forgot to remove them or didn't give enough ♥♥♥♥♥. This is very disappointing, there's clearly a lack of respect for artists and it's especially condemnable for a game that supposedly cares so much about environmental storytelling. 

2) The game just isn't even that fun.
Probably more interesting on multiplayer, but the single player mode feels kind of bland. You spend most of the time of the missions walking around aimlessly, and walking is really not an enjoyable experience. It's extremely slow and it feels clunky. 

3) The story
It's just... not good. Most of the missions feel very uninspired. That's all there is to say really.

Overall, not recommended. Especially for this price.

citations.review_text: Fresh install of windows on a new PC. Can't play the game with friends and they can't join me. Connection to host timed out.

I absolutely love this game playing in single player but as soon as you try and do anything with multiplayer it is basically impossible to play. Both me and my friend tried hosting the lobby (me pc, him on xbox) but there was no way it was play able, with the latency. Who ever was not the host would have a latency of well over 200-500ms , this is the only game that does this when we play together so I know its not an internet problem. I really do want to love this game but it hard to love a game that fights you when you want to play with friends.

YES! I absolutely recommend, it's a completely new gaming approach experience for me when you actually need to avoid pressing the trigger. Skipping the whole AI side I am having a blast on multiplayer with friends, the maps are swarmed with fun details and easter eggs, really appreciating that. We've had a few host disconnects despite having a steady internet connection, but willing to forgive that just for the general experience. claims.claim: Reviewers experience game crashes during missions.

citations.review_text:
i am really enjoying this game. it's truly so much fun and there are so many missions, loadout combinations, and an admirable amount of realism. it's funny at times, tense and scary at others. it's a blast and one of my favorite games i've played in awhile.

that said, the bugs in this game are inexcusable. ESPECIALLY at a $50 price tag. i cannot recommend it for that reason alone. normally when i see reviews talking about bugs i just brush them off thinking it can't be [i] that [/i] bad.... well it is that bad. it has also crashed on my friends and i SEVERAL times during missions which is incredibly annoying. i'm not even sure if the developers are patching them as i am finding reddit threads from months and even years ago talking about the same bugs i am currently experiencing. 

i also find the obvious use of undisclosed AI art to be disappointing to say the least. for a game that has made an estimated 300-400 MILLION, you'd think they'd take a fraction of that to hire real artists... it just sucks seeing developers resort to AI. call it what you will but it's lazy. even a competition among the players to utilize their artistic skills and put the winning art in the game + their name in the credits would be amazing. it doesn't have to cost anything. they seem to be really community involved so i think that is a realistic solution. all in all, there are no excuses for AI art in games.

tldr; fun but for $50 can't recommend due to bugs and ai art :(

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as having visual censorship and altered content compared to earlier versions.

citations.review_text:
It was obvious that this is just a matter of time before the game featuring "otherness" turns into just another nonsense, and it seems it happened right after I decided to take a break from it a little more than a year ago.

Not only is the game now visually censored, but features an automatic "kill switch" for when you're shooting a suspect after they've surrendered, even if all your team only has rubber bullets (so a console death, then). Some might say it's something to excuse the realism, but there is nothing "real" in immediately executing a squad leader by his teammates over a suspect's death (before that they would only kill you when you shot at them), or in censoring nudity, and other stuff in the game, either, so I doubt that.

I was happy to see myself right when opening it again today. In a world where regulations and political correctness rules, there is no place for anything, even art, to be truly "free" of them, and it is something that I understand. But when there is a choice in playing something that is free of aforementioned restrictions, or not, I prefer the obvious - even if it's mechanically, or visually aged, which isn't necessarily the case.

Also, if you grow weed, you are a psychopatic lunatic that tortures and kills cops, even in a legal US state. What a bunch of fиcking geeks.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that suspect AI can shoot players through walls or tiny gaps with high precision.

citations.review_text:
I bought a key for the digital deluxe version for $30, a great deal!

I love this game, especially modded!

There are a decent amount of creative maps in the in-game mod loader, I think I will start getting some more from mod.io

The vanilla game is challenging, and entertaining.
I find the campaign mode is quite a grind, but if you can get through it you'll be very good at the game!

I will probably end up modding it so that the enemy and team AI is better, they can be annoying. The enemies can detect you and shoot you without turning to aim at you, for instance.

There are some maps where the 360*, hyper aware enemy AI will see and shoot you through a tiny crack, or through brush textures that the player can't see through.

I really enjoy the game, even with it's faults! It's just fun!

Overall I recommend the game I really enjoy the fact that you can play any way you want. Also is a great game with friends and will test your patience and coordination. I believe as far as real tactical simulator is among the best out there. Maybe the AI should receive some updates because sometimes it feels invincible and has insane aim assist and wallhacks.
the ai is prime beaulo, pixel peeks you from across the map and you cant do anything while your ai teammates are lowk stupid, other than that its a good game

cohorts.summary: Long-term veterans praise the detailed tactical mechanics despite encountering paid downloadable content barriers, physics glitches, and hyper-accurate suspects.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as featuring detailed environments, gunplay, and mechanics with a slow-paced tactical style.

citations.review_text: While it has its bugs and quirks, this game has been amazing. It has a handful of great storylines which I personally enjoy in my games as a lore nerd. Even without the storytelling, the gunplay, mechanics and the maps on this game are very detailed, realistic and fun to play. I highly recommend this to any fan of tactical shooters, especially if it is one of your first tac shooters. The game is kinda hard on you but thats part of the appeal.

Ready or Not is an amazing game. Gameplay loop and visuals are great. I love how slow paced it is, how satisfying it feels to headshot a suspect that is holding a civilian hostage or when you enter a room expecting maybe one armed suspect but encounter 3 or 4 and manage to come up on top nonetheless. These are the kind of experiences that make Ready or Not live rent free in my mind and memory.

Sadly this game also suffers from many (very solvable) issues that seem to be neglected for a long time. To give you some examples, the friendly SWAT AI accompanying you while you play the game in singleplayer are so unbelievable incompetent and competent at the same time, it completely makes you loose any form of trust you placed initially into them. Their performance ranges from entering an open field and successfully incapacitating 10 suspects while outnumbered and outgunned to all of them running into rooms in reverse with a gun in their hand that they are out of ammo for. 

Free lean is another feature that is great in its fundamental concept but very badly implemented. Free lean offers you to lean on the horizontal plane in all directions giving you fine grained control over the exact angle you hold a corner or how you peak just slightly over cover. Its a lot of fun until you ever so slightly touch any object with a collision box (e.g. your AI SWAT mates that have no concept of spacing) leading to you getting pulled out of the specific angle you positioned yourself in, ideally while you are shooting as this causes your AI mates to raise their guns as well it seems. 

Visibility is another major issue in this game. The lighting selected for many scenes in this game looks only cinematic but falls so so far from anything playable. You will find yourself not being able to spot enemies that seem to pick you up visually without the slightest issue, making you avoid many areas in maps simply because you will not be able to spot enemies effectively.

I would love to see this ga…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that DLC add-ons cost extra money and lock missions behind paywalls.

citations.review_text: One of the better CQB styled games on the market. There are slight bugs here and there such as weapons going under carpet/ground textures making it difficult to secure evidence for a perfect score. But other than that this is a go to game for realistic and action-packed S.W.A.T missions. MOD-IO mods make for a MORE realistic approach to the game. Can't say I'm too happy with the lack of added maps for those who really don't want to pour funds into DLCs though.

Ready or Not is the mixture of a video game for both larpers and dedicated strategists that want a cool tactical shooter to look forward towards (even though its mostly for larpers that want to friendly fire their own friends)
Game itself, in its core without modding offers replayability to a degree where it could be considered enjoyable for a certain period of time
When you play and finish majority of the missions on a higher grade, there's essentially nothing to do in the later stages of the game besides changing loadouts and striking for better and faster records for missions.

I feel like when Void Interactive began adding in DLC's, it felt like them wanting to grab more money from their fanbase versus actually adding in newer content (guns, accessories and proper new missions) without having to relay on transactions for new content
Sure, they have given us free weapons but locking their community new missions and aesthetics behind a paywall is arguably dumb, given the fact we haven't gotten an update without it being DLC in well over a year or two (Give or take, I don't keep count of updates)

Despite development setbacks and arguably concerning criticism for the game's wicked AI system that can basically one-tap you in a mission and the overflowing number of DLC content that's a leeway for you  to unlock more stuff to do, it's a pretty fun shooter game with your friends where you just wanna mess around

Get it on sale or I don't know watch youtubers play the game lol
